papers.title_zh: 小肺结节更少 vs 更密集随访的非劣效性：整群随机务实试验未能证实非劣效，且更少随访组≥20 mm晚期肺癌比例更高
papers.title_en: Less Versus More Intensive Strategies for Follow-up of Small Pulmonary Nodules : A Cluster Randomized Pragmatic Clinical Trial.
papers.authors: Gould MK, Kelly K, Qi L, Creekmur B, de Bie E, Aberle DR, Dyer DS, Mazzone PJ et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Health Systems Science, Kaiser Permanente Bernard J.
papers.results: 27个月内确诊肺癌：较少密集组273/17 841（1.5%），更密集组231/16 845（1.4%）。有可用数据的肺癌患者中，诊断时>20 mm者：较少密集组97/267（36.3%），更密集组62/224（27.7%）。校正后，较少密集组检出的>20 mm肺癌更多，差异为7个百分点（95% CI，-2.0至15.9个百分点），超过预设的5个百分点非劣效界值，但未达统计学显著。局限性：依从性欠佳、检验效能有限、残余混杂。
papers.authors_conclusion: Small, malignant pulmonary nodules frequently progress during follow-up. Although neither follow-up strategy was clearly superior, these data raise concerns about the less intensive recommendations for follow-up of small nodules.
papers.ai_note: 非劣效性未达成：点估计7个百分点已超过预设5个百分点界值，95% CI（-2.0至15.9）跨越0且上界远超界值，故本试验既不能宣称非劣效，也不能判定优效，结论方向不确定；作者结论将此表述为'raise concerns'而非明确的非劣效失败，措辞偏向警示。主要终点分析限定于'有可用数据的肺癌患者'（267/273与224/231），即以随机化后的癌症发生这一中间事件为条件进行选择性分析，存在选择偏倚风险且存在缺失数据。肺癌发生率本身在两组间几乎相同（1.5% vs 1.4%），提示'更少随访'未增加癌症检出但可能影响分期分布，该分期差异的临床意义缺乏生存终点支撑。摘要未报告各组实际随访依从性数值与失访情况，信息不足。

pico.p: 24个美国医院与医疗系统集群内的34 686例新发肺结节（≤15 mm，偶然发现或筛查发现）患者；50.8%为女性，平均年龄64.5岁（SD 11.7）
pico.ic: 较少密集随访方案（参照现行及既往Fleischner Society与Lung-RADS推荐） vs 更密集随访方案；主要终点为诊断时>20 mm肺癌所占比例，预设非劣效界值5个百分点

papers.reason: 直接影响≤15 mm偶然发现或筛查检出肺结节的随访频率选择与Fleischner/Lung-RADS降强度推荐的采纳判断；其非劣效未达成的整群随机证据可作为结节随访指南修订与降强度策略质疑的对照基线。
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The current less intensive guidelines for pulmonary nodule follow-up have not been compared with more intensive strategies. OBJECTIVE: To determine whether less intensive follow-up of small pulmonary nodules is noninferior to more intensive follow-up. DESIGN: Unblinded, cluster randomized, pragmatic comparative effectiveness trial. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT02623712). SETTING: 24 clusters of U.S. hospitals and health care systems. PARTICIPANTS: 34 686 patients with a new pulmonary nodule measuring 15 mm or less, detected incidentally or by screening. INTERVENTION: Follow-up protocols were modeled on current and prior recommendations from the Fleischner Society and the Lung CT Screening Reporting and Data System (Lung-RADS). Each cluster was randomly assigned to the less or more intensive follow-up protocol. MEASUREMENTS: The primary outcome was the proportion of lung cancers measuring more than 20 mm at diagnosis. Analyses were conducted using mixed-effects logistic regression. The prespecified noninferiority margin was 5 percentage points. RESULTS: A total of 34 686 participants (50.8% women) were enrolled, with a mean age of 64.5 years (SD, 11.7). Lung cancer was diagnosed within 27 months of nodule identification in 273 of 17 841 participants (1.5%) in the less intensive group and 231 of 16 845 (1.4%) in the more intensive group. Among participants with lung cancer with available data, 97 of 267 (36.3%) in the less intensive group and 62 of 224 (27.7%) in the more intensive group had cancers larger than 20 mm at diagnosis. After adjustment, more lung cancers larger than 20 mm were identified with less intensive screening (7 percentage points [95% CI, -2.0 to 15.9 percentage points]), exceeding the noninferiority margin but not statistically significant. LIMITATIONS: Suboptimal adherence, limited power, and residual confounding. CONCLUSION: Small, malignant pulmonary nodules frequently progress during follow-up. Although neither follow-up strategy was clearly superior, these data raise concerns about the less intensive recommendations for follow-up of small nodules. PRIMARY FUNDING SOURCE: Patient-Centered Outcomes Research Institute.

papers.reason: 影响晚期SCLC患者接受tarlatamab治疗的生物标志物分层与耐药后治疗策略判断；同时为按TF亚型设计前瞻性转化队列、选择组织/液体活检检测指标提供分层框架与机制依据
papers.abstract_en: Although small cell lung cancer (SCLC) comprises transcription factor (TF)-defined molecular subtypes (ASCL1, NEUROD1, and POU2F3), whether these predict therapeutic response or evolve under therapeutic pressure remains unclear. Tarlatamab, a DLL3 × CD3 bispecific T cell engager, has transformed SCLC therapy, yet responses are heterogeneous and resistance develops in most patients. We inferred tumor gene expression from circulating chromatin in patient plasma and developed an immunocompetent syngeneic mouse model to study tarlatamab response and resistance. Across patients and mice, TF subtypes associated with response or resistance. ASCL1 tumors were enriched for response, consistent with DLL3 being an ASCL1 target gene, while NEUROD1 tumors had inferior responses and POU2F3 tumors were intrinsically resistant. Acquired resistance involved selection for a NEUROD1-high state with downregulation of the ASCL1-linked antigen DLL3 or enrichment of regulatory and exhausted T cell programs. These findings support TF-defined subtypes as clinically relevant frameworks for understanding tarlatamab response and resistance in SCLC.

papers.authors: Carvalho ARS, Guimarães AR, Kee SL, Martins da Fonseca J, Zhang JMF, Pickhardt PJ, Braithwaite D, Perchiazzi G et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: D'Or Institute for Research and Education, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil; Department of Radiology, University of Florida, Gaine…
papers.results: ELCSC：检出异常肺功能AUROC 0.898，敏感度89.9%，特异度66.1%；COPDGene：AUROC 0.913，敏感度66.9%，特异度96.3%；外部队列FEV1、FVC、FEV1/FVC的CCC为0.80-0.88。留出开发数据：完整模型CCC 0.86/0.85/0.71，仅影像模型0.83/0.82/0.50，仅特征模型0.55/0.65/0.35。COPD亚组（FEV1/FVC<0.70）CCC 0.62伴系统性高估；低FVC、保留比值模式亚组CCC 0.70-0.78
papers.authors_conclusion: 该模型可在独立队列无需重训地估测肺功能参数并检出异常肺功能，在相同决策规则下呈现不同的敏感度-特异度组合；对既有CT的机会性评估显示出前景，但转诊表现因人群而异，前瞻性效用尚未证实
papers.ai_note: 同一决策规则下两个外部队列敏感度差异显著（89.9% vs 66.9%）、特异度反向（66.1% vs 96.3%），提示阈值不可跨人群迁移，摘要强调AUROC接近而弱化该落差；训练参照为支气管舒张前肺量计而COPDGene参照为舒张后，参照标准不一致可能影响一致性解读；COPD亚组存在系统性高估且CCC降至0.62，模型在目标异常人群中表现最弱；摘要提及做了prevalence-conditional predictive values评估但未报告具体数值——信息不足；无前瞻性临床效用验证

pico.p: NLST 5,975名参与者的10,371次低剂量CT重建用于训练；外部验证为External Lung Cancer Screening Cohort（ELCSC, n=268）与COPDGene（n=10,302次扫描）
pico.ic: 干预：三维CNN融合20项肺密度与气管几何定量特征的混合模型估测FEV1、FVC、FEV1/FVC并检出异常肺功能；对照：影像单独模型与特征单独模型的消融比较，参照标准为肺量计（NLST为支气管舒张前，COPDGene为支气管舒张后）

papers.reason: 为机会性CT肺功能评估的算法研发提供跨队列外部验证基线与消融证据，影响肺筛人群中气流受限初筛与是否进一步行肺量计检查的决策路径设计，同时其亚组失效模式为同类模型的验证方案（亚组一致性、阈值迁移性）提供对照
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Spirometry is underused and most airflow obstruction remains undiagnosed. Chest CT acquired for lung cancer screening contains anatomical and densitometric information that may proxy lung function. RESEARCH QUESTION: Can a deep learning model combining volumetric CT with CT-derived quantitative features estimate spirometric parameters and detect abnormal spirometry in independent external cohorts without retraining? STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: A three-dimensional convolutional neural network trained on 10,371 low-dose CT reconstructions from 5,975 National Lung Screening Trial (NLST) participants was fused with 20 lung densitometry and tracheal geometry features to predict FEV1, FVC and FEV1/FVC. The frozen model was applied to an External Lung Cancer Screening Cohort (ELCSC, n = 268) and COPDGene (n = 10,302 scans). Ablation, two spirometric-pattern subgroups and prevalence-conditional predictive values were also evaluated. Reference spirometry was pre-bronchodilator in NLST and post-bronchodilator in COPDGene. Abnormal spirometry (FEV1/FVC < 0.70, FEV1 < 80% or FVC < 80% predicted) was assessed with sensitivity, specificity and AUROC, and agreement with the concordance correlation coefficient (CCC). RESULTS: The model detected abnormal spirometry with AUROC 0.898 (sensitivity 89.9%, specificity 66.1%) in the ELCSC and AUROC 0.913 (sensitivity 66.9%, specificity 96.3%) in COPDGene, with CCCs of 0.80-0.88 for FEV1, FVC and FEV1/FVC. In held-out development data, CCCs were 0.86/0.85/0.71 (full model) versus 0.83/0.82/0.50 image-only and 0.55/0.65/0.35 feature-only. Agreement was lower, with systematic overestimation, in a COPD subgroup (FEV1/FVC < 0.70; CCC 0.62) and in a low-FVC, preserved-ratio pattern (CCC 0.70-0.78). INTERPRETATION: The model estimates spirometric parameters and detects abnormal spirometry across independent cohorts without retraining, with different sensitivity-specificity profiles at the same decision rule. It shows promise for opportunistic assessment of existing CT scans, but referral performance varies by population and prospective utility is unproven. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: COPDGene, ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT00608764.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: First-line treatments for advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) without actionable mutations include immunotherapy (IO) and/or chemotherapy. The NRG-LU002 randomized phase II trial evaluated the addition of local consolidative therapy (LCT)-radiation and/or surgery-to maintenance systemic therapy (MST) in oligometastatic NSCLC. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Patients with metastatic NSCLC and up to three residual extracranial metastatic sites (excluding primary) showing stable disease or partial response after four courses of first-line therapy were randomly assigned 1:2 to MST alone or LCT followed by MST. LCT permitted included stereotactic body radiation therapy, hypofractionated radiation, and/or surgery. Stratification was by histology and IO use. The primary end point was progression-free survival (PFS), with secondary end points including overall survival (OS), quality of life, and toxicity. RESULTS: From April 2017 to November 2021, 215 patients (81 MST and 134 LCT + MST) enrolled at 68 sites (median age 65 years, 78% nonsquamous histology, 90% IO-based therapy). Median follow-up was 21.9 months. PFS rates at 1 and 2 years, respectively, were 48.0% and 35.9% (MST) versus 51.5% and 40.1% (LCT + MST), with a hazard ratio (HR) of 0.93 (P = .66). Among IO-treated patients, PFS HR was 0.90. OS HRs were 1.05 for both all patients and IO subgroup. Grade ≥2 adverse events were more frequent in LCT + MST (84% v 73%, P = .05), including grade ≥3 pneumonitis (10% v 1%, P = .02). Early pneumonitis was linked to worse PFS/OS. Longer MST (>6 months) correlated with improved outcomes by landmark analyses. Liver metastases and poor performance status predicted worse prognosis. CONCLUSION: Adding LCT to IO-based first-line therapy in oligometastatic NSCLC did not improve PFS or OS. Increased toxicity from local treatment reduced MST administration, affecting outcomes. Further refinement of patient selection is needed to optimize LCT therapeutic ratios.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Obesity is common in chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH), but comparative data on haemodynamic recovery, biomarker kinetics and functional outcomes after pulmonary endarterectomy (PEA) remain limited. OBJECTIVES: To compare haemodynamic, biomarker, functional and perioperative outcomes by obesity status after PEA. METHODS: Single-centre cohort of 202 consecutive patients undergoing PEA for CTEPH (January 2015-February 2024), stratified by BMI (obese ≥30 kg/m², n = 62; non-obese, n = 140). Serial biomarkers were analysed using log-transformed linear mixed-effects models (LMM; group × time interaction as primary test, Bonferroni-corrected contrasts). Haemodynamics were compared by ANCOVA adjusted for baseline, cardiac index using BSA (Mosteller), and NYHA class by exact test and adjusted logistic regression. RESULTS: The LMM group × time interaction was significant only for CK-MB [F(4; 669.3)=2.67; p = 0.031]; the single Bonferroni-significant contrast was at ∼24 h (geometric mean 42.2vs 29.3 ng/mL; p = 0.012). Troponin [F(4; 538.4)=1.69; p = 0.151] and CPK [F(4; 685.9)=1.13; p = 0.341] interactions were not significant. Postoperative cardiac index (2.70 vs 2.74 L/min/m²; p = 0.77) and ANCOVA-adjusted ΔPVR (p = 0.39) did not differ. Postoperative NYHA class I was less frequent in obese patients (47.8%vs 70.8%; adjusted OR 0.45, 95% CI 0.21-0.99). Cumulative mortality at 30 days was 9.7% in obese and 11.4% in non-obese patients (p = 0.81). CONCLUSION: In this single-centre observational cohort, obesity was not associated with significant differences in postoperative haemodynamics, length of stay or short-term mortality, although estimates were imprecise. Obese patients less often achieved NYHA class I. These hypothesis-generating findings do not support excluding patients from PEA evaluation on the basis of BMI alone.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: This study aims to establish a deep learning model based on interactive 3D segmentation to predict NICT efficacy. METHODS: This study collected 517 NSCLC patients who underwent NICT and surgery at three centers. VISTA3D is applied in this study for CT images to achieve automatic tumor identification in NSCLC patients via automated segmentation combined with point prompts. Multiplex immunofluorescence was performed to compare the tumor immune microenvironment between low-risk and high-risk patients stratified by the model. Based on this model, patients likely to benefit from adjuvant immunotherapy are identified. RESULTS: This model attained AUC values of 0.83 and 0.81 for cohort A and C, with a Dice coefficient reaching 0.83 ± 0.14. Patients identified as high-risk by the model showed a potential survival advantage with adjuvant immunotherapy (HR: 0.55 for DFS; HR: 0.51 for OS). Exploratory multiplex immunofluorescence analysis suggested compositional differences in the tumor immune microenvironment between risk groups. CONCLUSION: The deep learning model developed in this study, based on interactive segmentation, achieves comparable performance to manual segmentation and assists clinicians in effectively predicting pCR in NSCLC patients undergoing NICT prior to surgical treatment. Furthermore, adjuvant immunotherapy was associated with improved survival in high-risk patients, requiring prospective validation.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: For patients with locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer (LA-NSCLC), NRG-RTOG 0617 found that non-adaptive radiation therapy (naRT) dose escalation to 74 Gy worsened overall survival (OS) vs. 60 Gy, while NRG-RTOG 1106 showed PET-adapted RT (aRT) dose escalation was safe. This study compares aRT vs. naRT in LA-NSCLC. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Patients from RTOG 0617 and 1106 randomized to dose-escalation arms with PET-based staging were included. All received thoracic radiotherapy with concurrent and consolidation carboplatin/paclitaxel without immunotherapy. Outcomes were OS, progression-free survival (PFS), cumulative incidence of local-regional progression (CILRP), and grade 3+ toxicity. Results were adjusted for baseline differences between cohorts. Cox models evaluated survival and logistic regression models evaluated toxicity outcomes. RESULTS: Eighty-four patients received aRT and 184 received naRT (median nominal dose 71 Gy vs. 74 Gy). naRT patients had better performance status (Zubrod 0 58% vs. 44%, p=0.0390 and less Intensity Modulated Radiotherapy (IMRT) (49% vs. 92%, p<0.0001). aRT had lower lung V20 (30% vs. 32%, p=0.0413), mean esophagus dose (27Gy vs. 29Gy, p=0.0017), and trend to lower heart V40 (8% vs. 10%, p=0.0907). Unweighted, aRT had a trend to higher 3-year OS (39% vs. 27%, HR=0.72, 95% CI 0.52-1.01, p=0.0535) and significantly higher CILRP (36% vs. 49%, HR = 0.64, 95% CI 0.43 - 0.95, p=0.0324), with similar PFS (20% vs. 21%, HR=0.95, 95% CI 0.71-1.27, p=0.7214). Weighted analyses showed similar outcomes between cohorts. aRT had lower grade 3+ esophagitis (6% vs. 22%, OR=0.24, 95% CI 0.09-0.63, p=0.0040) and similar hematologic toxicity (36% vs. 33%, OR=1.15, 95% CI 0.66-1.99, p=0.6257). Weighted models confirmed these findings and showed lower grade 3+ pneumonitis (OR=0.114, 95% CI 0.01-0.98, p=0.0478) and cardiotoxicity (OR=0.114, 95% CI 0.01-0.98, p=0.0478) for aRT. CONCLUSION: aRT had improved CILRP and a trend to improved OS with significantly reduced toxicity and improved dosimetry vs. naRT.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) improve cancer outcomes but can cause respiratory complications, including acute respiratory failure (ARF). While checkpoint inhibitor pneumonitis (CIP) is a recognized immune-related pulmonary toxicity that can lead to ARF, not all ARF in ICI-exposed patients is CIP. We sought to characterize ARF etiologies after ICI exposure and compare outcomes between CIP and non-CIP ARF. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of ICI-treated adults with ARF, defined as ≥ 24 hours of invasive or noninvasive ventilatory support within 2 years of first ICI, across 5 hospitals (2017-2024). ARF etiology was determined by physician chart review; those with potential CIP underwent multidisciplinary adjudication. The association between CIP versus non-CIP ARF and 90-day mortality was evaluated using multivariable Cox models. RESULTS: Among 197 ICI-treated patients, CIP was determined to be the primary etiology in 29 (15%) ARF cases, while 168 (85%) had other etiologies (eg, pneumonia, progressive cancer). At ARF onset, CIP patients were more hypoxemic but exhibited less multiorgan dysfunction. Ninety-day mortality was 66% versus 71% and was not different in adjusted models (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 0.66; 95% CI, 0.40-1.08; P = .10), but CIP was associated with lower in-hospital mortality (aHR 0.43; 95% CI, 0.21-0.88; P = .02). Among survivors, 13% restarted ICI (5% adjudicated CIP vs. 17% adjudicated non-CIP patients; P = .28). CONCLUSION: Most ARF after ICI therapy was not attributable to CIP. Better in-hospital survival with CIP did not translate into improved 90-day survival, suggesting ARF etiology may shape early clinical trajectory. These findings highlight the importance of accurate etiologic attribution.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) exhibits high heterogeneity in response to immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy. The identification of predictive biomarkers that are easily applicable and minimally invasive is therefore of great interest. METHODS: Baseline peripheral blood samples from real-world stage IV NSCLC patients treated with first-line pembrolizumab were analyzed using high-dimensional single-cell mass cytometry, clustering, and machine learning according to their response to ICI therapy. Functional immune characterization was additionally performed for validation. RESULTS: We observed significantly higher frequencies of circulating CD4⁺ and CD8⁺ EMRA T cells, defined as terminally differentiated effector memory cells re-expressing CD45RA (CD45RA⁺CCR7⁻), in non-responder patients to programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) inhibitors. Upon in vitro stimulation, EMRA T cell subsets from non-responders showed reduced expression of activation markers and effector molecules, including CD25, CD69, IFN-γ, and GZMB. Based on these findings, we developed the CD4⁺ EMRA ImmunoPredict Score (CEIPS), a simplified predictive model that integrates activation and regulatory markers of CD4⁺ EMRA T cells. CEIPS stratified patients into Low- and High-Risk groups, with the latter showing significantly poorer progression-free and overall survival (p = 0.005 and p < 0.001, respectively). CONCLUSIONS: Peripheral CD4⁺ and CD8⁺ EMRA T cells are associated with anti-PD-1 immunotherapy response in metastatic NSCLC patients and represent clinically feasible blood-based biomarkers to improve patient stratification. Building on these findings, we developed the CEIPS score, which integrates these biomarkers and demonstrates predictive value for immunotherapy outcomes in NSCLC. The findings presented here support the potential value of CEIPS as a candidate predictive biomarker; however, validation in larger independent multicenter cohorts will be required before clinical implementation.

papers.abstract_en: Sixty years after its initial description, acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) remains defined by bilateral radiographic opacities and impaired oxygenation rather than by its underlying biology. This syndromic definition encompasses considerable clinical and biological heterogeneity, which may contribute to the ineffectiveness of pharmacotherapy trials to date. Subphenotyping aims to address this heterogeneity by identifying more homogeneous patient groups that differ in prognosis and/or treatment response. In this narrative review, framed by the research questions outlined in the 2023 European Society of Intensive Care Medicine guidelines, we synthesize current approaches to ARDS subphenotyping across complementary domains: clinical (etiology, rapidly improving ARDS), physiological (gas exchange, recruitability, elastance, and ventilatory ratio), morphological (focal versus non-focal radiological patterns), and biological (individual injury biomarkers and the hyperinflammatory and hypoinflammatory subphenotypes). We examine their pathobiological basis, temporal dynamics, and retrospective evidence for heterogeneity of treatment effect, and consider how parsimonious biomarker panels, machine-learning classifiers, and adaptive basket trial designs may support clinical implementation. Prospective validation across diverse populations, including resource-limited settings, remains a key priority.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Patients with stage III epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) may be considered unresectable because of mediastinal nodal disease or invasion of adjacent structures. We evaluated whether EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (EGFR-TKI)-based induction therapy could enable conversion surgery in selected patients with initially unresectable disease. PATIENTS AND METHODS: We retrospectively identified 162 consecutive patients with initially unresectable stage IIIA-N2b to IIIC EGFR-mutant NSCLC who received EGFR-TKI-based induction therapy between January 2017 and December 2022. After induction, 70 patients were considered technically resectable by multidisciplinary reassessment. Of these, 42 chose conversion surgery and 28 declined surgery and continued non-surgical treatment. Perioperative outcomes, pathologic response, downstaging, event-free survival (EFS), and overall survival (OS) were evaluated. Inverse probability of treatment weighting was used to reduce measured confounding. RESULTS: All 42 surgical patients underwent video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery without conversion to thoracotomy. R0 resection was achieved in 41 patients (97.6%). Major pathologic response was observed in 13 patients (31.0%), including 1 patient (2.4%) with pathologic complete response. Lymph-node downstaging occurred in 25 patients (59.5%). After weighting, conversion surgery was associated with longer EFS and OS than non-surgical treatment. CONCLUSION: In this selected retrospective cohort, conversion surgery after EGFR-TKI-based induction was feasible and was associated with longer EFS and OS than continued non-surgical treatment. This investigational strategy requires prospective validation before routine use.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality, and acute exacerbations substantially increase disease burden. Although numerous prediction models have been developed to estimate the risk of future exacerbations, their predictive performance and methodological quality remain uncertain. OBJECTIVE: To systematically review and meta-analyze multivariable prediction models for estimating the risk of future acute exacerbations among patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. METHODS: Six electronic databases were searched from inception to May 20, 2026. Studies developing or validating multivariable models for predicting future exacerbations were included. C-statistics were pooled using a random-effects meta-analysis after logit transformation. Between-study heterogeneity was assessed using the I 2 statistic and 95% prediction intervals. Exploratory subgroup and restricted analyses were conducted to further investigate heterogeneity, and risk of bias was assessed using the Prediction Model Risk of Bias Assessment Tool. RESULTS: Twenty-nine studies involving more than 1.08 million patients with COPD were included in the systematic review, of which 17 contributed to the meta-analysis. The pooled C-statistic was 0.75 (95% confidence interval 0.70-0.79), with substantial between-study heterogeneity (I 2 = 97%). Exploratory subgroup analyses identified a statistically significant difference in discrimination according to exacerbation severity (P = 0.040). Substantial heterogeneity persisted in an exploratory restricted analysis of three studies predicting severe exacerbation-related events over approximately 12 months. Overall, 26 studies were judged to be at high risk of bias, primarily in the Analysis domain. CONCLUSION: Prediction models for future acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease showed variable discriminative performance, while substantial between-study heterogeneity and widespread risk of bias limit confidence in the pooled estimate and its clinical applicability. Further research should prioritize standardized prediction tasks, rigorous model development, transparent reporting of calibration and model specifications, independent external validation, and evaluation of clinical utility.

papers.abstract_en: IMPORTANCE: A multidimensional chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) diagnostic schema incorporating imaging and clinical features beyond airflow obstruction has been proposed. However, its implications for prevalence, case composition, and prognostic stratification in the general population remain unknown. OBJECTIVE: To compare the population-level classification and prognostic implications of a multidimensional COPD diagnostic schema with those of the Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease (GOLD) definition. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This population-based cohort study used the Swedish Cardiopulmonary Bioimage Study, conducted at 6 Swedish university hospitals 2013-2018 to compare diagnostic definitions in the full cohort and in a symptom-restricted subgroup approximating routine clinical practice, with mortality follow-up through September 30, 2024. Randomly sampled adults aged 50 to 64 years with complete classification data, including postbronchodilator spirometry and chest computed tomography assessment of emphysema and bronchial wall thickening were included. EXPOSURE: Classification according to the multidimensional COPD diagnostic schema and an operationalized GOLD definition. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: COPD prevalence, case composition, and all-cause mortality. RESULTS: A total of 29 281 participants (15011 females [51.3%]; mean [SD] age, 57.5 [4.3] years) were included; 1347 participants (4.6%) met multidimensional COPD criteria. In analyses restricted to 6016 symptomatic individuals, prevalence was similar under the multidimensional and GOLD definitions (909 [15.1%] vs 853 [14.2%]), but case composition differed. Approximately one-third of patients with multidimensional COPD (281 of 909 [30.9%]) did not meet the GOLD criteria. Across the full cohort, 438 individuals (32.5% of multidimensional COPD cases) were asymptomatic and would be unlikely to undergo diagnostic evaluation in routine symptom-driven care. During follow-up, 634 deaths occurred. Among symptomatic participants, adjusted mortality risk was increased in multidimensional-only cases (hazard ratio [HR], 2.58; 95% CI, 1.66-4.01) and those meeting both definitions (HR, 2.20; 95% CI, 1.59-3.04), but not in patients with GOLD-only COPD (HR, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.44-2.00). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this population-based cohort study, COPD prevalence was similar with a multidimensional COPD diagnostic schema to that obtained using GOLD criteria, but case composition differed substantially. The multidimensional schema identified increased mortality risk among individuals not captured by GOLD, suggesting improved prognostic stratification, while the identification of many asymptomatic cases highlights an existing detection gap in current symptom-driven care pathways.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Hypophosphatemia is common in critical illness, but whether prompt phosphate repletion improves patient-centered outcomes remains uncertain. OBJECTIVE: To estimate the effect of phosphate repletion within 12 hours of incident hypophosphatemia on 28-day ventilator-free days. METHODS: In this target trial emulation using MIMIC-IV 3.0, adults during their first ICU stay with an initial serum phosphate concentration <2.5 mg/dL within 48 hours of ICU admission were eligible. Treatment strategies were repletion within 12 hours versus no repletion within that grace period, with follow-up beginning at the 12-hour landmark. Stabilized inverse probability weighting was used to estimate average treatment effects on the primary outcome of 28-day ventilator-free days. RESULTS: Among 14,823 eligible patients, 6,995 received early repletion and 7,828 did not. Weighted covariate balance was adequate, with a maximum absolute standardized mean difference of 0.059. Early phosphate repletion did not improve 28-day ventilator-free days (MD -0.12 days, 95% CI -0.43 to 0.18, p = 0.424), ICU-free days, mortality, or renal replacement therapy. Among patients with repeat phosphate measurements, early repletion was associated with higher odds of phosphate normalization (OR 1.37, 95% CI 1.24-1.50) and hyperphosphatemia (OR 1.35, 95% CI 1.03-1.76). CONCLUSION: In this target trial emulation of critically ill adults, early phosphate repletion promoted biochemical normalization without improving patient-centered outcomes, suggesting selective rather than routine early repletion.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: PESI and ESC risk classification are widely used for early risk stratification of acute pulmonary embolism (PE). The Composite PE Shock (CPES) score has been proposed to better identify normotensive shock. We compared the prognostic performance of PESI, ESC risk class, and CPES. METHODS: We performed a retrospective chart review of consecutive adults with acute PE managed by PERT (PE Response Team) at three teaching hospitals within the Mount Sinai Health System from January 2020 through June 2024. Multivariable logistic regression was used to predict 30-day mortality. Discrimination was assessed using area under the receiver operating characteristic (AUROC) curves. Net Reclassification Improvement (NRI) and Integrated Discrimination Improvement (IDI) were calculated to assess incremental utility of CPES over PESI and ESC risk class. RESULTS: A total of 404 patients were included (median age: 65 years; 223 [55.2%] women). Median PESI and CPES scores were 82 (IQR: 66-104) and 3 (IQR: 2-4). ESC risk stratification was as follows: low: 12 (3.0%), intermediate low: 71 (17.6%), intermediate high: 235 (58.2%), and high-risk: 86 (21.3%). AUROC for predicting 30-day mortality of PESI, ESC risk class, and CPES were 0.706, 0.643, and 0.420 respectively, and for a two-index model (PESI + ESC), and the full model (PESI + ESC + CPES) were 0.650, and 0.722, respectively. Relative to the two-index model, the full model increased specificity by 10% and decreased sensitivity by 3.7% (NRI: 6.3%, IDI: 1.3%), consistent with modest incremental reclassification. The strongest incremental signal for CPES was observed for receipt of advanced reperfusion therapy, where addition of CPES to PESI and ESC increased AUROC from 0.664 to 0.775. CONCLUSIONS: In a contemporary PERT cohort of patients with acute PE, CPES performed poorly as a standalone predictor of 30-day mortality but provided modest conditional incremental information when added to PESI and ESC risk classification. CPES showed a stronger association with receipt of advanced reperfusion therapy, suggesting that it may capture shock physiology relevant to escalation decisions.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Uptake of pulmonary rehabilitation (PR) in COPD patients is low. This study evaluated the use of PR in patients with severe COPD and identified predictive factors of participation in a PR program. METHODS: A post hoc analysis of data from a large cohort of patients with severe COPD (FEV1< 50% predicted) included in a cross-sectional multicenter study conducted in Spain. The characteristics of patients referred to PR were compared to those of non-participants in a PR program. Variables independently associated with referral PR program were evaluated using bivariate analysis and a logistic regression model. RESULTS: Of the total 4800 patients, 2080 (43%) were receiving non-pharmacological treatment, with 482 (23%) of them enrolled in a PR program. The uptake rate of PR was 10%. COPD-related variables significantly associated with referral to PR included poor COPD control, two or more exacerbations in the past year, degree of dyspnea, and degree of airflow impairment. Education and psychological support, nutritional treatment, tobacco cessation support, CPAP, home oxygen therapy, and domiciliary assisted ventilation were significantly associated with referral to PR. Other significant variables: ex-smoking condition, good/moderate adherence to inhaled therapy, living in an urban/semiurban area, and receiving specialized care by a pulmonologist. CONCLUSION: In this real-world study of severe COPD patients, the uptake of PR was only 10%. Educational and psychological support together with nutritional treatment and smoking cessation support should be emphasized as these factors were significant predictors of PR. Overall, PR is underutilized and concentrated in patients with more severe airflow impairment.

papers.results: 识别出2个分子簇：Cluster 2（n=38）BALF淋巴细胞、CD8+ T细胞、IL-6及全身炎症标志物升高，富集OP影像模式及免疫介导ILD（CTD-ILD/IPAF/CIP）；Cluster 1（n=44）以UIP模式和慢性纤维化IIP为主。非IPF患者中Cluster 2免疫抑制治疗应答率91.4%，Cluster 1为46.2%。通路分析示Cluster 2补体与淋巴细胞活化上调、Cluster 1补体与固有免疫通路抑制；两簇共同下调RNA代谢、氧化还原稳态与细胞骨架组织相关通路。UFD1、RPS20、MGP、RAVER1被一致优先为纤维化ILD进展相关候选标志物。

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Interstitial lung disease (ILD) heterogeneity complicates management, and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) proteomics may enable molecular subtyping. We sought to define BALF-based molecular subtypes across common ILDs, examine their clinical correlates, and identify biomarkers predicting treatment outcomes in fibrotic ILDs. METHODS: Eighty-two treatment-naïve ILD patients were prospectively enrolled, including chronic fibrosing idiopathic interstitial pneumonias (IIPs), connective tissue disease-associated ILD (CTD-ILD) and/or interstitial pneumonia with autoimmune features (IPAF), hypersensitivity pneumonitis (HP), and checkpoint inhibitor-associated pneumonitis (CIP), together with 14 controls. BALF proteins were quantified by data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry. Unsupervised k-means clustering, enrichment, correlation, and machine-learning analyses were performed. RESULTS: Two distinct molecular clusters were identified. Cluster 2 (n = 38) had higher BALF lymphocytes, CD8+ T cells, interleukin-6, and systemic inflammatory markers, and was enriched for organizing pneumonia patterns and immune-mediated ILDs (CTD-ILD/IPAF/CIP). Cluster 1 (n = 44) was predominantly associated with usual interstitial pneumonia patterns and chronic fibrosing IIPs. Among non-idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis patients, 91.4% in Cluster 2 responded to immunosuppressive therapy compared with 46.2% in Cluster 1. Pathway analysis showed upregulated complement and lymphocyte activation in Cluster 2, and suppressed complement and innate immune pathways in Cluster 1. Both clusters shared downregulation of ribonucleic acid metabolism, redox homeostasis, and cytoskeletal organization. UFD1, RPS20, MGP, and RAVER1 were consistently prioritized as candidate biomarkers associated with progression in fibrotic ILD. CONCLUSIONS: BALF proteomics identified two molecular endotypes reflecting inflammatory activation and suppression. Shared defects in cellular homeostasis may represent a common pathogenic basis for ILD.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) remains the metric for grading obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) severity, although its association with cardiovascular (CV) outcomes is inconsistent. Hypoxic burden (HB) integrates the depth and duration of respiratory event-related oxygen desaturations and may better reflect OSA-related physiological stress. We evaluated the association between HB and CV outcomes and its prognostic information relative to AHI. METHODS: We conducted a systematic review according to PRISMA 2020 recommendations and the Synthesis Without Meta-analysis (SWiM) guideline. PubMed, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to August 2026. The primary synthesis included independent cohort-level estimates reporting adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) per 1-standard deviation (SD) increase in HB, which were presented in a forest plot without a pooled estimate and synthesized by direction of effect. Within-study HB and AHI associations were compared descriptively. RESULTS: Eleven publications reporting 14 analyses from seven cohorts or trials were included. Four independent cohort-level estimates were available for the primary synthesis. All four indicated higher CV risk with increasing HB (HRs per 1-SD increase 1.13-1.45); the 95% CI excluded the null in three estimates and reached it in the fourth. Given the small number of estimates, these were not pooled. In a descriptive synthesis of eight within-study comparisons, HB showed a significant positive association with CV outcomes, whereas AHI showed no consistent positive association and was inversely associated with CV mortality in one MrOS analysis. In a single post hoc analysis of RICCADSA, high HB was associated with increased MACCE risk even among participants with relatively low AHI. CONCLUSIONS: Across individual community-based cohorts and populations with established cardiovascular disease and OSA, higher HB was consistently associated with increased CV morbidity and mortality, with modest effect sizes, and may provide prognostic information not fully captured by AHI. Given the small number of independent cohorts and the descriptive nature of the synthesis, these findings should be regarded as hypothesis-generating. These findings support a pathophysiologically informed, multidimensional assessment of OSA severity and CV risk. Prospective studies should standardize HB measurement, establish actionable thresholds, validate incremental prognostic value, and determine whether HB-guided risk stratification improves clinical outcomes.

papers.authors: Hirakawa T, Yamaguchi K, Miura S, Shimoji K, Sakamoto S, Horimasu Y, Masuda T, Nakashima T et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Molecular and Internal Medicine, Graduate School of Biomedical and Health Sciences, Hiroshima University, …
papers.results: 特发性AE-IPF在2年内发生率为10.1%；化疗触发AE-ILD在1年内发生率为26.9%。ROC分析：特发性AE-IPF截断值16.7 ng/mL（AUC 0.65；敏感度55.6%；特异度81.3%）；化疗触发AE-ILD截断值15.2 ng/mL（AUC 0.69；敏感度92.9%；特异度47.4%）。高基线S100A9组较低基线组的特发性AE-IPF发生率更高（25.0% vs. 5.8%，p = 0.012），化疗触发AE-ILD发生率更高（39.4% vs. 5.3%，p = 0.008）。以死亡为竞争事件的探索性多变量Fine-Gray回归分析显示，高基线S100A9水平与特发性AE-IPF及化疗触发AE-ILD的发生显著相关（摘要未给出HR及95%CI）。
papers.authors_conclusion: 高基线血清S100A9水平可能与特发性AE-IPF和化疗触发AE-ILD风险增加相关。
papers.ai_note: AUC仅0.65与0.69，判别力中等偏低，且截断值在同一队列内产生、无外部验证；化疗触发AE-ILD的特异度仅47.4%，与92.9%的敏感度高度不对称，阳性预测价值存疑。Fine-Gray回归标注为exploratory，摘要未报告HR、95%CI与具体协变量。单中心回顾性设计，事件数少（IPF队列约9例事件），统计效能有限。两个队列疾病背景、随访时长（2年 vs 1年）与终点定义不同，结果不宜合并解读。摘要未说明采血时点与化疗周期的时序关系、未报告S100A9连续变量分析，亦无校准度或增量价值（如C-index变化）评估。信息不足：无独立验证队列。

papers.reason: 为IPF及ILD患者急性加重风险分层提供候选基线生物标志物证据，其截断值与判别效能可作为后续前瞻性验证研究的样本量与设计参考；同时提示化疗前ILD患者的急性加重风险评估仍缺乏高精度工具。
papers.abstract_en: BackgroundIdiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a representative form of interstitial lung disease (ILD). Acute exacerbation of IPF (AE-IPF), categorized as idiopathic or triggered, can be fatal, similar to acute exacerbations observed in other forms of ILD. S100A9, a damage-associated molecular pattern, has been associated with poor prognosis in IPF and higher mortality in patients with AE-IPF. However, its association with the development of AE, particularly in idiopathic or triggered cases, remains unclear.ObjectivesThis study evaluated the association between baseline serum S100A9 levels and the development of idiopathic AE-IPF and chemotherapy-triggered AE-ILD.DesignThis was a single-center retrospective study of two independent cohorts: an IPF cohort and a cohort of ILD concomitant with lung cancer.MethodsWe analyzed 89 patients diagnosed with IPF between June 2005 and December 2020 and 52 patients with ILD concomitant with lung cancer who received cytotoxic chemotherapy between July 2010 and December 2021 at Hiroshima University Hospital. Baseline serum S100A9 levels were quantified using an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay.ResultsIdiopathic AE-IPF occurred in 10.1% of patients within two years, and chemotherapy-triggered AE-ILD occurred in 26.9% within one year. ROC analysis identified baseline serum S100A9 cut-off values of 16.7 ng/mL for idiopathic AE-IPF (AUC 0.65; sensitivity 55.6%; specificity 81.3%) and 15.2 ng/mL for chemotherapy-triggered AE-ILD (AUC 0.69; sensitivity 92.9%; specificity 47.4%). Patients with high baseline serum S100A9 levels had significantly higher incidences of idiopathic AE-IPF and chemotherapy-triggered AE-ILD than those with low levels (25.0% vs. 5.8%, p = 0.012; 39.4% vs. 5.3%, p = 0.008, respectively). In exploratory multivariable Fine-Gray regression analyses with death as a competing event, high baseline serum S100A9 levels were significantly associated with the development of idiopathic AE-IPF and chemotherapy-triggered AE-ILD.ConclusionHigh baseline serum S100A9 levels may be associated with an increased risk of idiopathic AE-IPF and chemotherapy-triggered AE-ILD.

papers.abstract_en: While microwave ablation (MWA) is established as a safe and effective treatment for lung cancer, incomplete MWA (iMWA) paradoxically promotes a pro-tumorigenic immunosuppressive microenvironment that accelerates residual disease progression. This study aims to elucidate the cellular mechanism by which iMWA induces systemic immunosuppression, specifically through remodeling the immune landscape of the spleen and tumor-draining lymph nodes (TdLNs) in a Lewis lung carcinoma (LLC) model. Our findings provide insights for developing novel immunomodulatory strategies for lung cancer patients following iMWA. Compared with the control and MWA groups, iMWA significantly elevated the proportion of immunosuppressive cells in both the spleen and TdLNs, as evidenced by increased frequencies of CD8⁺ PD-1⁺ T cells, myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs), and regulatory T cells (Tregs). Concurrently, iMWA induced mild activation of effector immune cells, characterized by a slight upregulation of effector memory T (TEM) cells, conventional type 1 dendritic cells (cDC1s), and major histocompatibility complex class I (MHC-I) expression on cDC1s. In summary, iMWA primarily establishes an immunosuppressive microenvironment within the spleen and TdLNs in lung cancer, while simultaneously triggering a weak activation of effector immune responses. These findings provide a theoretical basis for developing combinatorial strategies to reverse immunosuppression following iMWA, thereby improving the prognosis of lung cancer patients.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: Wearable devices enable convenient assessment of sleep in daily life. Smart rings facilitate long-term monitoring; however, their agreement with electroencephalography (EEG)-based sleep assessment remains unclear. We evaluated the performance of the SOXAI RING -derived sleep parameters against those obtained using a portable EEG device. METHODS: Of 52 university students enrolled, 49 (mean age 19.3 years; 42 females) were included in the final analysis. Participants underwent simultaneous overnight monitoring with the SOXAI RING (SOXAI Co., Ltd.) and portable EEG device (Proassist Co., Ltd.) under habitual home sleeping conditions. Total sleep time (TST), sleep onset latency (SOL), wake after sleep onset (WASO), and sleep stages were compared between devices. Epoch-by-epoch (EBE) analyses were also performed to evaluate sleep-wake and four-stage sleep classification. RESULTS: A strong correlation for TST was observed between devices (ρ = 0.70, p < 0.01). Bland-Altman analysis showed that the SOXAI RING tended to underestimate TST and light sleep, while overestimating WASO and deep sleep. In EBE analysis, the SOXAI RING showed high sensitivity for sleep but low specificity for wake. For four-stage classification, the overall accuracy was 50.0% and Cohen's κ was 0.27. CONCLUSIONS: The SOXAI RING showed good performance for estimating TST and may be useful for long-term sleep monitoring under habitual home conditions. However, EBE analysis demonstrated limited performance for wake detection and sleep-stage classification. Sleep-stage estimates and sleep fragmentation metrics should therefore be interpreted cautiously, and further refinement of sleep-staging algorithms is warranted.

papers.title_en: CT-Derived Skeletal Muscle Metrics and Clinical Features for Predicting 1-Year Readmission After AECOPD: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
papers.authors: Long H, Zheng C, Zhan Z, He Z, Li Q, Pang J, Zhang K, Li Y et al.

papers.results: 1年内再入院60/192（31.3%）。Ridge模型患者水平ROC-AUC 0.746，PR-AUC 0.620，Brier 0.183，校准截距-0.002、斜率1.86（Hosmer-Lemeshow P=0.211）。既往住院为最强预测因子（OR=1.775，95%CI 1.453-2.284）；T12_ESMA越大再入院几率越低（OR=0.742，95%CI 0.541-0.961）。加入4项CT肌肉指标与黏液栓评分后ΔAUC +0.017（95%CI -0.018 to 0.054），连续NRI 0.406（95%CI 0.107-0.711），IDI 0.014（95%CI 0.001-0.028）。预设探索性分析中黏液栓负担修饰T12_ESMA关联（交互P=0.002），评分≥3时关联更强（OR=0.403，95%CI 0.221-0.734）。
papers.authors_conclusion: In this single-centre cohort, a Ridge model combining CT-derived skeletal muscle metrics with routine clinical variables showed moderate discrimination, with no evidence of gross miscalibration. T12_ESMA is a candidate imaging biomarker derivable from routinely acquired CT. Its incremental value lay in reclassification rather than discrimination, and the modifying effect of mucus plug burden was exploratory. External and prospective validation are required.
papers.ai_note: 信息不足/疑点：(1) 校准斜率1.86明显偏离理想值1，提示模型可能过拟合，作者以Hosmer-Lemeshow P=0.211主张'无明显失校准'，属对校准指标的选择性解读；(2) ΔAUC的95%CI跨0（-0.018 to 0.054），判别增量无统计学意义，文章转而突出连续NRI/IDI显著——连续NRI已知易产生假阳性增量，为主要终点（判别）阴性后以次要/替代指标立论；(3) 13种算法同批比较后以预设Ridge为主模型可部分缓解选择偏倚，但60个事件、单中心、仅内部验证，样本量对多变量模型偏小；(4) 黏液栓交互为预设探索性分析且未见多重比较校正，交互P=0.002与亚组OR需外部验证；(5) 摘要未给出外部验证或校准曲线细节，外部/前瞻性验证结论仅停留在作者声明。

pico.ic: CT骨骼肌指标（T12_ESMA等4项）+黏液栓评分+临床变量的Ridge模型 vs 仅临床变量模型；另比较13种算法

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: Patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) face persistently high readmission rates after an acute exacerbation (AECOPD). We developed and internally evaluated a model predicting 1-year readmission from CT-derived skeletal muscle metrics combined with routine clinical variables. METHODS: We retrospectively enrolled 192 inpatients with AECOPD. T12 erector spinae area (T12_ESMA), L1 rectus abdominis area, and low-attenuation pectoralis and T4 muscle areas were measured on non-contrast chest CT. Thirteen algorithms were compared using repeated 5-fold cross-validation, with Ridge logistic regression pre-specified as the primary model. Discrimination, calibration, decision curves and the incremental value over a clinical-only model were assessed. RESULTS: Among 192 patients, 60 (31.3%) were readmitted within 1 year. The Ridge model reached a patient-level ROC-AUC of 0.746, PR-AUC 0.620 and Brier score 0.183, with calibration intercept -0.002 and slope 1.86 (Hosmer-Lemeshow P=0.211). Prior hospitalisation was the strongest predictor (OR=1.775, 95% CI 1.453-2.284), and a larger T12_ESMA was associated with lower readmission odds (OR=0.742, 95% CI 0.541-0.961). Adding the four CT muscle metrics and the mucus plug score to a clinical-only model left discrimination almost unchanged (ΔAUC +0.017, 95% CI -0.018 to 0.054) but improved reclassification (continuous NRI 0.406, 95% CI 0.107-0.711; IDI 0.014, 95% CI 0.001-0.028). In a pre-specified exploratory analysis, mucus plug burden modified the T12_ESMA association (interaction P=0.002), which was stronger when the score was ≥3 (OR=0.403, 95% CI 0.221-0.734). CONCLUSION: In this single-centre cohort, a Ridge model combining CT-derived skeletal muscle metrics with routine clinical variables showed moderate discrimination, with no evidence of gross miscalibration. T12_ESMA is a candidate imaging biomarker derivable from routinely acquired CT. Its incremental value lay in reclassification rather than discrimination, and the modifying effect of mucus plug burden was exploratory. External and prospective validation are required.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Spilled gallstones following laparoscopic cholecystectomy are an uncommon and likely underdiagnosed complication. Their delayed presentation and challenging radiological identification may result in diagnostic delays. This study aimed to assess their clinical presentation, diagnosis, and management, with particular emphasis on minimally invasive approaches. METHODS: A retrospective analysis of a prospective single-center cohort of patients treated for complications secondary to spilled gallstones following cholecystectomy between January 2019 and December 2024 was performed, and the results were compared with the available literature. A specific percutaneous drainage protocol was used with a dual therapeutic and localization purpose. RESULTS: Seventeen patients were included, with a median age of 72 years (53-87). The median time to symptom onset was 13 months. Abdominal pain was present in 94.1% of patients and fever in 70.6%. Right-sided pleural empyema due to transdiaphragmatic extension developed in 41.2%. Spilled gallstones were identified on preoperative imaging in 64.7% of cases. Percutaneous drainage was performed in 64.7%, and 16 patients (94.1%) underwent definitive surgical treatment. Of the 16 surgically treated patients, 14 (87.5%) were initially approached laparoscopically, with 13 procedures completed laparoscopically (92.9%). Spilled gallstones were identified intraoperatively in 8 patients (50%). Two recurrences occurred, with no mortality. CONCLUSIONS: Complications from spilled gallstones may present late and involve both the abdominal and thoracic cavities, even when the stones are not identified on imaging. Percutaneous drainage may provide both initial source control and anatomical guidance during reoperation. When surgical treatment is required, a laparoscopic approach is feasible in most patients.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: To evaluate the association between time-updated enteral feeding intolerance (EFI) states and in-hospital mortality in mechanically ventilated critically ill patients. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed adults receiving mechanical ventilation who remained in the ICU for at least 3 days. EFI was assessed daily during Nutrition Days 1-7. Patients initially contributed person-time to the no-EFI state, entered the first-EFI state on the first qualifying EFI day, and entered the recurrent-EFI state on the second qualifying day. In-hospital death was the event, and alive discharge was censored. The primary Cox model adjusted for age, sex, APACHE II score, and septic shock, included an APACHE II score-by-log(time + 1) interaction, was stratified by baseline AKI, and used patient-level cluster-robust standard errors. RESULTS: Among 447 patients, 132 died in hospital. By final cumulative status, 248 (55.5%) had no EFI, 68 (15.2%) had single-day EFI, and 131 (29.3%) had recurrent EFI. In the time-updated Model A, no independent association was observed between the first-EFI state and in-hospital mortality (aHR 1.12, 95% CI 0.66-1.90). The recurrent-EFI state was associated with higher mortality than the no-EFI state (aHR 2.30, 95% CI 1.55-3.43) and the first-EFI state (aHR 2.06, 95% CI 1.20-3.54). One-day-lag analysis retained the recurrent-versus-no-EFI association, whereas the recurrent-versus-first-EFI contrast was nonsignificant. CONCLUSION: The recurrent-EFI state was associated with higher in-hospital mortality, although its contrast with first EFI was sensitive to exposure timing. Recurrent EFI may serve as a longitudinal marker for clinical reassessment, although residual confounding and the composite EFI definition preclude causal interpretation.

papers.abstract_en: The ion channel-forming natural product amphotericin B (AmB) can serve as a molecular prosthetic for the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) anion channel and thereby restore host defenses in cultured cystic fibrosis (CF) airway epithelia. This is despite the fact that the permeability of AmB-based channels favors cations, and these channels lose their capacity to increase airway surface liquid (ASL) pH in CF airway epithelia at high concentrations. We hypothesize that modifying such channels to favor anion permeability would increase their capacity to restore physiology in disease-relevant model systems compared to AmB. Here we show that a synthetic derivative of AmB, AmB-AA, which has an added positively charged appendage and forms ion channels with an improved relative permeability to anions, outperformed AmB in increasing the ASL pH in CF airway epithelia at both low and high concentrations. Further modifications led to another AmB derivative, C2'epiAmB-AA, that minimize cholesterol binding and thus toxicity to cultured CF airway epithelia and was an effective surrogate for CFTR in primary cultured airway epithelia from people with CF.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Dupilumab, an interleukin-4 (IL-4) receptor α antagonist, which blocks IL-4 and interleukin-13 (IL-13) signaling, has demonstrated effectiveness in treatment of severe asthma in randomized trials. However, there is limited data in real world settings, particularly among racially and ethnically diverse pediatric populations that are disproportionately affected by severe asthma. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effectiveness of dupilumab among children with severe asthma. METHODS: In a retrospective cohort study of 37 children with severe asthma treated with dupilumab for ≥ 6 months, we quantified change in asthma control test (ACT) score, systemic corticosteroid use, hospitalization rates, PICU admission rates, and spirometric parameters over the ≥ 6-month follow-up period. Dupilumab was the first biologic used in all included patients. We also assessed Asthma clinical remission at 12 and 24 months, defined as an ACT score ≥ 20, pre-bronchodilator FEV1 ≥ 80% predicted, and no exacerbation requiring systemic corticosteroids or asthma-related hospitalization. RESULTS: The study included 74% Hispanic pediatric patients. The baseline ACT score was 15.5 ± 4.8. The ACT score improved at first follow-up to 19.6 ± 4.8 (p < 0.001). Mixed-effects modeling demonstrated progressive improvement, with adjusted mean ACT increases of 3.81 (95% CI 1.84-5.78), 5.02 (2.69-7.36), and 8.17 (5.55-10.79) points at 6-11, 12-23, and 24-35 months, respectively (all p < 0.001). Systemic steroid courses decreased by 2.7-3.0 courses per year across phases (p ≤ 0.03). The hospitalization rate decreased from 0.78 admissions per patient-year before dupilumab initiation to 0.13 admissions per patient-year during post-treatment follow-up (p < 0.001). The pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) admission rate decreased from 0.24 to 0.05 admissions per patient-year after dupilumab initiation (p = 0.013). Forced expiratory volume in 1 s/forced vital capacity (FEV1/FVC) improved significantly by 9.54% (95% CI 4.88-14.20, p < 0.001) at 24-35 months. Asthma remission was achieved in 22.2% and 38.5% of patients after a 1-year and 2-year follow-up, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Dupilumab resulted in sustained asthma control, reduced systemic steroid exposure, and progressive improvement in airflow obstruction among children with severe asthma.

papers.abstract_en: Irregular sleep is associated with negative health and performance outcomes, including cardiovascular disease and impaired attentional performance. Young adults with unmanaged sleep disorders may be particularly vulnerable to health and safety risks associated with irregular sleep, but sleep regularity in this group is not yet well-characterized. This study describes sleep regularity in young adults with unmanaged sleep disorders relative to healthy sleepers. Seventy-two young adults (60% female; Age [mean ± SD] = 25.1 ± 4.6 years) recorded sleep-wake patterns using daily diaries over 7-21 days. Sleep disorder diagnoses were confirmed by trained clinicians using the Structured Clinical Interview for Sleep Disorders (Revised; SCISD-R), diagnostic polysomnography and validated questionnaires (e.g., Insomnia Severity Index, Epworth Sleepiness Scale). Sleep regularity was quantified using the Sleep Regularity Index (SRI). Bootstrapped regressions were used to compare SRI between sleep disorder types and healthy sleepers. Of the sleep disorder groups examined, only individuals with Delayed Sleep-Wake Phase Disorder (DSWPD) exhibited significantly lower SRI (Median SRI (IQR): 75.8(66.6-80.7)) than healthy sleepers (79.4(76.0-85.0)), B = -8.4, 95% CI[-15.5, -2.1]. There was a trend towards lower SRI in individuals presenting with DSWPD comorbid with Obstructive Sleep Apnea (72.2(66.0-78.2)), B = -10.5[-25.0, 2.1]; and Insomnia (78.2(69.7-81.1)), B = -3.6[-8.9 to 2.0]. Lower sleep regularity in young adults with DSWPD likely reflects a misalignment between biological sleep timing and external obligations (e.g., early morning commitments). Regularizing sleep-wake timing may be a worthwhile target in DSWPD treatment. Further research is warranted to consider the effect of targeted sleep regularity interventions in this population alongside existing treatment recommendations. papers.abstract_en: Respirable crystalline silica is a classical fibrogenic occupational dust, but accumulating evidence increasingly places it among the environmental exposures capable of influencing systemic immune tolerance. This review asks a single question: does silica exposure contribute to the development of systemic autoimmune rheumatic disease, and how convincing is the evidence for each disease? The evidence is not uniform, and the diseases are therefore ranked rather than grouped. It is most persuasive for rheumatoid arthritis, where nationwide cohorts with quantitative exposure assessment, pooled analyses, a dose-response gradient and a reproducible interaction with smoking in seropositive disease all point the same way, and almost as persuasive for systemic sclerosis, which shows the largest effect estimates and a long clinical lineage but a strong dependence on how exposure is defined. Support weakens for systemic lupus erythematosus, where an association is probable at high exposure but the magnitude is uncertain and the literature is markedly heterogeneous, and weakens further for antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-associated vasculitis, where older case-control findings are tempered by a recent null result in a large renal cohort. The inflammatory myopathies are an emerging signal that concerns phenotype rather than incidence. Evidence is sparse for Sjögren disease, sparser for mixed connective tissue disease and overlap syndromes, and absent for psoriatic arthritis and spondyloarthritis. Two problems run through the field. Autoantibody positivity in exposed workers is far more common than classified disease and has never been followed prospectively to it, and silicosis has often been used as a surrogate for exposure when it is better understood as a consequence and possible mediator of it. Mechanisms are biologically plausible without establishing disease-specific causality. Pulmonary implications matter for diagnosis, and prospective cohorts of exposed workers are the research priority.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: A next-generation SARS-CoV-2 vaccine must address the currently inadequate prevention of virus transmission, particularly against emerging variants of concern, a challenge that none of the licenced commercial vaccines fully meet. Effective control of respiratory pandemics necessitates vaccines that 1) can be rapidly adapted, 2) have high patient compliance with simple and non-invasive administration, and 3) block transmission following virus challenge. METHODS: We describe the characterization of an updated single-cycle SARS-CoV-2 vaccine candidate (scVac), engineered as a replication-defective virus with targeted deletions of the E gene and ORF6 and ORF7a, together with a truncation of ORF3a. The candidate carries an Omicron XBB.1.5 Spike (scVacXBB), while maintaining all essential antigenic properties. Safety was evaluated in K18-hACE2 transgenic mice, the most sensitive virulence model, and immunogenicity and efficacy were assessed in the Syrian hamster model. FINDINGS: The vaccine was well tolerated in K18-hACE2 transgenic mice, with no clinical signs or adverse events observed. In Syrian hamsters, scVacXBB induced potent systemic and mucosal immune responses, together with a strong neutralising antibody response. Notably, no virus transmission to co-housed naïve animals was detected in the scVac-vaccinated group. In contrast, transmission was observed in the bivalent Omicron mRNA vaccine comparator group under the conditions tested. INTERPRETATION: Our results demonstrate that scVacXBB-induced immunity not only prevents disease but also transmission in a prime-boost hamster direct-contact model following homologous XBB.1.5 challenge. Furthermore, the successful incorporation of the XBB.1.5 Spike protein into the scVac frame supports its potential for adaptation to emerging variants. These findings highlight the potential of this single-cycle vaccine concept as a next-generation COVID-19 vaccine, offering robust protection, effective interruption of transmission, and a favourable tolerability observed in the evaluated animal models. FUNDING: Research was funded by the German Research Foundation, an Innosuisse grant, and by RocketVax AG.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Lymphangioleiomyomatosis (LAM) is a rare, progressive neoplastic lung disease. Lymphocytes play a central role in tumor immunity. However, circulating lymphocyte count and function have not been studied yet in sporadic LAM. METHODS: Two-sample Mendelian randomization (TSMR) analysis was used to estimate the causal effect of circulating lymphocyte count on sporadic LAM. Circulating lymphocyte subsets were quantified, and inhibitory receptors (PD-1, LAG-3, TIM-3, and CTLA-4) on T cells were measured in a clinical cohort. CD4⁺ and CD8⁺ T cells were isolated and cultured to measure cytokine expression including IFN-γ and IL-4, followed by PD-1 blockade experiments using an anti-PD-1 antibody. RESULTS: TSMR analysis showed lower circulating lymphocyte count was associated with a higher risk of sporadic LAM. Circulating lymphocytes, mainly T cells instead of B and NK cells, were significantly decreased in sporadic LAM. Reduced CD8⁺ T cell count was significantly correlated with VEGF-D, CT gradings and FEV1% pred. The expression of PD-1, but not LAG-3, TIM-3, or CTLA-4, was significantly increased on both CD4⁺ and CD8⁺ T cells. The frequency of IFN-γ but not IL-4 producing CD4⁺ and CD8⁺ T cells was significantly decreased in sporadic LAM. PD-1 blockade restored the frequency of IFN-γ producing CD4⁺ and CD8⁺ T cells at least in part. CONCLUSIONS: Our data indicate that circulating lymphocytes, mainly T cells, are associated with the development of sporadic LAM. T cell exhaustion occurs in the peripheral blood of patients with this disease. Immune checkpoint blockade therapy may be a new strategy for sporadic LAM.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The Australian cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk calculator (AUS-CVD-RC) was developed to improve CVD risk prediction in Australians, and launched in 2023. We tested the validity of the AUS-CVD-RC with long-term atherosclerotic vascular disease (ASVD) risk in a cohort of community-dwelling older women. METHODS: The study included 905 older women (70 to <80 years of age) from Western Australia recruited in 1998 (baseline). Women with chronic kidney disease and prevalent ASVD were excluded. AUS-CVD-RC were calculated at baseline and grouped into low (<5%), moderate (5% to <10%) and high (≥10%) risk. Atherosclerotic events, comprising hospitalisations and/or deaths, over 5, 10, and 14.5 years were obtained from linked health records. RESULTS: Over 5 years, 9.3% of women experienced an ASVD-related event, increasing to 21.1% and 37.0% at 10 years and 14.5 years, respectively. Compared to women with low risk, those with moderate (hazard ratio [HR] 2.89 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.32-6.32) and high risk (HR 6.34 95% CI 2.64-15.23) had greater hazards for an ASVD-related event over 5 years. Similar associations were observed at 10 and 14.5-years. Unadjusted event rates (%) over 5 years by AUS-CVD-RC risk groups were: low 7.4 (95% CI 3.0-15.3); moderate 20.3 (95% CI 15.5-26.2); and high risk 42.7 (95% CI 25.3-67.4). Despite this, the predictive utility for AUS-CVD-RC and ASVD events over these three different follow-up periods had an area under the curve of <0.70. CONCLUSIONS: We demonstrate the AUS-CVD-RC identifies community-dwelling older women with a higher risk of ASVD, a population where risk prediction remains challenging. Future research should explore if the inclusion of women-specific factors may improve prognostic performance.

papers.abstract_en: Given the critical role of recovery after sleep loss in many professional settings, this scoping review analysed studies linking the structure of recovery sleep to cognitive restoration in sleep-deprived healthy adults. In accordance with PRISMA guidelines, four electronic databases were searched using keywords covering three concepts: acute sleep deprivation/restriction, neurocognitive performance, and recovery sleep. Eligible studies measured sleep parameters during recovery, from a brief nap to several nights, following total sleep deprivation or sleep restriction, using objective monitoring (actigraphy or polysomnography), and assessed cognition objectively. Paediatric, adolescent and elderly populations were excluded. A total of 31 studies were included, with considerable heterogeneity in design. The main sleep parameters were total sleep time and markers of homeostatic regulation (slow-wave sleep duration and slow-wave activity), and the main cognitive domains were sustained attention and memory. Total sleep time emerged as the most important factor for cognitive recovery after sleep deprivation/restriction, though recovery also depended on recent sleep history. Slow-wave activity and sleep microstructure may explain interindividual differences in restoration. Most associations, however, rely on group-level comparisons rather than interindividual correlations, and the cognitive functions studied remain limited. Further studies should assess correlations between sleep parameters and cognitive recovery and improve reproducibility.

Regularly monitoring lung function is crucial for these people to guide appropriate treatment and establish prognosis. Shifting disease monitoring and diagnostic testing from clinic to home could provide advantages to patients with ALS and other advanced stage chronic conditions who have complex care needs. OBJECTIVE: To explore Veteran and provider perspectives of a home spirometry program. DESIGN AND PARTICIPANTS: We conducted semi-structured interviews with providers in ALS clinics and Veterans living with ALS who participated in a home spirometry program at two VA medical centers. APPROACH: Our team used the Practical, Robust Implementation and Sustainability Model (PRISM) to guide our conventional content analysis and thematic analysis. KEY RESULTS: We generated four main patterns and themes: benefits and challenges, suggestions for the future, empowering patients to take charge of their health and trusting the results of home spirometry and care providers. papers.abstract_en: Research into emotional processes in insomnia disorder is growing, yet more studies are needed on patients' emotional functioning. This study investigates emotional responses of individuals with insomnia disorder and healthy controls to dynamic emotional stimuli related and unrelated to insomnia. The assessment incorporates physiological, subjective, and behavioural measures of emotional reactivity. The study involved 97 patients with insomnia disorder, 49 healthy controls under moderate sleep restriction, and 47 healthy controls without sleep restriction. In a controlled laboratory setting, participants watched an insomnia-related and a sadness-related video clip. Emotional reactivity was assessed through facial electromyography (EMG), self-report, and coding of video-recorded facial expressions. The spontaneous use of emotion regulation strategies was also assessed. The emotional responses to the two video clips in the three groups were compared in multiple MANCOVAs with emotion-related assessments as dependent variables. EMG revealed a distinct pattern in insomnia patients, showing higher zygomatic and lower corrugator muscle activity during the insomnia-related compared to the sadness-related video clip. Only patients with insomnia disorder reported a pre-to-post video clip increase in arousal in response to the insomnia-related clip. The findings indicate a unique engagement of patients with insomnia when processing emotional stimuli related to their condition. More research using multi-method approaches is needed to differentiate the effect of sleep restriction from that of chronic insomnia disorder. Strategies aimed at addressing emotional processes may prove beneficial in modulating emotional responses to symptoms-related stimuli.

papers.abstract_en: Lung cancer is one of the most prevalent malignant tumors globally, with high incidence and mortality rates. Despite continuous advancements in targeted therapy and immunotherapy, tumor heterogeneity and acquired drug resistance remain significant limitations to treatment efficacy. In recent years, metabolic reprogramming has been recognized as one of the core hallmarks of tumorigenesis and progression, prompting a shift in cell death research from traditional apoptosis models to metabolism-driven regulatory mechanisms. Metabolically regulated cell death modalities-such as ferroptosis, cuproptosis, and disulfide stress-induced cell death have gradually emerged as research hotspots. Furthermore, lysosomal zinc toxicity-induced cell death (zincotoxicity) and alkaliptosis expand the theoretical boundaries of this field. This review focuses on lung cancer as the research context, with particular emphasis on non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), which accounts for the majority of cases, and systematically summarizing the molecular mechanisms and regulatory networks of the aforementioned metabolic cell death pathways, as well as their functional variations across different subtypes. Special emphasis is placed on analyzing the pivotal roles of key metabolic nodes including metal ion homeostasis, the GSH/NADPH buffering system, and mitochondrial function in multi-pathway crosstalk. Additionally, the review explores the contributions of non-coding RNAs, epigenetic modifications, and post-translational regulation to the development of anti-death phenotypes, along with their clinical translational potential. Targeting the metabolic cell death network is expected to provide novel theoretical foundations and intervention strategies for overcoming drug resistance and optimizing therapeutic approaches in lung cancer.

papers.title_zh: 六个月婴儿习惯性同床睡眠与活动记录仪静息-活动节律无关联：横断面研究
papers.title_en: Bed-sharing and actigraphic rest-activity rhythms in six-month-old infants: a cross-sectional study.
papers.authors: Lacerda V, Buest de Mesquita Silva R, Pykocz AH, Santos JS, Beijamini F, Dos Santos GD, Louzada FM
papers.affiliation_highlight: Universidade Federal do Paraná, Av.
papers.results: 同床与任何静息-活动节律指标均无关联；调整后差异小且95%置信区间排除任一方向超过0.44个标准差的效应（RA 0.009，95% CI -0.014至0.032；IS -0.007，-0.038至0.024；IV 0.003，-0.044至0.050；L5 -27.5 counts/min，-76.2至21.2；M10 -57.1 counts/min，-343.4至229.2）。在进一步调整母亲年龄、母乳喂养、光照暴露、母亲就业、婴儿睡眠困难及月龄后结论不变；限制于可比记录时长、单胎和足月婴儿的分析中结论亦不变。探索性对比中，同床不一致的婴儿（偶尔或频繁，n=40）M10高于同床安排一致（从不或总是）的婴儿。
papers.authors_conclusion: 习惯性同床与六个月婴儿的活动记录仪静息-活动节律无关联。该估计排除了中等或大的差异但不排除小的差异，且不支持关于昼夜节律机制的推论。
papers.ai_note: 主要终点全部为阴性，摘要以CI排除≥0.44 SD效应作为主要信息呈现，属对阴性结果的合理限定表述；但报告中夹带一项未预先设定的探索性对比（同床不一致n=40的M10更高），无具体数值与CI/P，存在被选择性强调的风险，且该对比无多重比较校正说明。暴露为家长报告的同床行为，存在分类与回忆偏倚；横断面设计无法确定时序与因果。样本量对小于0.44 SD的效应把握度不足，作者已明示。研究人群为巴西婴儿睡眠行为，与胸外科/胸部肿瘤业务无直接交集，临床外推有限。

pico.p: CPAPI出生队列（巴西里贝朗普雷图）194名六个月龄婴儿，平均月龄6.4个月（范围6.0–8.4），踝戴活动记录仪有效记录中位7.4天（2.8–12.2）
pico.ic: 频繁或总是同床（n=99）对比从不或偶尔同床（n=95），采用Mann-Whitney检验及按婴儿性别、社会经济状态调整的线性回归并作错误发现率校正

papers.reason: 作为高质量阴性研究范例，为'暴露与行为节律无中等以上关联'提供CI明确的证据模板，可参照其效应量排除与敏感性分析写法设计呼吸/睡眠相关阴性研究；对胸部肿瘤临床决策无直接影响。
papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: To examine whether habitual bed-sharing is associated with non-parametric rest-activity rhythm measures in six-month-old infants. METHODS: Cross-sectional analysis of 194 infants (mean age 6.4 months, range 6.0 to 8.4) from the CPAPI birth cohort, Ribeirão Preto, Brazil. Infants wore an ankle actigraph for a median of 7.4 valid days (2.8 to 12.2). Relative amplitude (RA), interdaily stability (IS), intradaily variability (IV), L5 and M10 were derived from non-binarized activity counts. Infants reported to share a bed frequently or always (n = 99) were compared with those sharing never or occasionally (n = 95) using Mann-Whitney tests and linear regression adjusted for infant sex and socioeconomic status, with false discovery rate correction. RESULTS: Bed-sharing was not associated with any rest-activity rhythm measure. Adjusted differences were small, with 95% confidence intervals excluding effects above 0.44 standard deviations in either direction (RA 0.009, 95% CI -0.014 to 0.032; IS -0.007, -0.038 to 0.024; IV 0.003, -0.044 to 0.050; L5 -27.5 counts/min, -76.2 to 21.2; M10 -57.1 counts/min, -343.4 to 229.2). Conclusions were unchanged after adjustment for maternal age, breastfeeding, light exposure, maternal employment, infant sleep difficulties and age, and in analyses restricted to comparable recording lengths, singletons and term infants. In an exploratory contrast, infants with inconsistent bed-sharing (occasionally or frequently, n = 40) had higher M10 than infants with consistent arrangements (never or always). CONCLUSION: Habitual bed-sharing was not associated with actigraphic rest-activity rhythm measures at six months. The estimates exclude moderate or large differences but not small ones, and do not support inferences about circadian mechanisms.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: To report a rare case of IgG4-related disease (IgG4-RD) with atypical predominant thoracic involvement mimicking lung cancer and sarcoidosis. CASE PRESENTATION: A 74-year-old male with a history of heavy smoking presented with chronic cough and exertional dyspnea for 1 year. Chest high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) revealed bronchovascular bundle thickening, a right parahilar mass, multiple perilymphatically distributed solid nodules, lymphadenopathy, and pleural effusion. Laboratory tests revealed marked elevations of serum IgG4 (6710 mg/dL) and IgE (2210 mg/dL). Histopathological examination of lung, pleural biopsy, and lymph node consistently demonstrated dense lymphoplasmacytic infiltration with abundant IgG4-positive plasma cells, without storiform fibrosis or obliterative phlebitis. The patient was definitively diagnosed with IgG4-RD via multidisciplinary team (MDT) consultation. Oral prednisone resulted in significant radiological improvement. CONCLUSIONS: IgG4-RD can mimic common thoracic disorders such as lung cancer and sarcoidosis. Early corticosteroid therapy is effective. An experienced MDT, integrating detailed clinical findings, serology, radiology, and histopathology, is essential for prompt diagnosis and timely intervention.

papers.authors: Arnal JM, Jacquin L, Khirani S
papers.affiliation_highlight: Service de Réanimation Polyvalente et Unité de Ventilation à Domicile, Hôpital Sainte Musse, Toulon, France.
papers.authors_conclusion: Ventilator settings are not directly interchangeable across NIV devices. Safe device transitions require individualized reassessment of patient-ventilator interaction using waveform analysis and clinical evaluation rather than relying on numerical equivalence alone.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Switching between home noninvasive ventilation (NIV) devices is common in clinical practice because of changes in patient needs, device availability, or product discontinuation. However, key ventilator settings are implemented differently across manufacturers, making direct transfer of settings challenging. OBJECTIVE: To compare the technical implementation of inspiratory trigger sensitivity, rise time, and cycling-off criteria across commonly used home NIV ventilators and provide practical guidance for safe transitions between devices. METHODS: Home NIV ventilators routinely used in adult and pediatric populations in Europe were reviewed. Technical specifications for inspiratory triggering, rise time, and cycling-off criteria were extracted from the ventilators technical and user manuals, and supplemented by direct communication with manufacturers when necessary. Settings were harmonized according to their physiological or algorithmic definitions rather than manufacturer-specific terminology and compared descriptively across ventilators, patient configurations, and circuit types. RESULTS: Substantial variability was identified in the implementation of these settings. Inspiratory triggering relies on either fixed flow thresholds or adaptive algorithms, with performance influenced by leaks, circuit configuration, and pediatric-specific algorithms. Rise time definitions differ considerably, with some manufacturers using fixed time-based settings and others employing relative pressurization algorithms, resulting in non-equivalent pressure delivery profiles. Cycling-off criteria vary due to flow-processing differences and proprietary algorithms despite similar settings. Consequently, identical values across ventilators do not ensure equivalent patient-ventilator interaction. CONCLUSIONS: Ventilator settings are not directly interchangeable across NIV devices. Safe device transitions require individualized reassessment of patient-ventilator interaction using waveform analysis and clinical evaluation rather than relying on numerical equivalence alone.
